# IEEE 1016

[IEEE 1016-2009](https://standards.ieee.org/standard/1016-2009.html),
*IEEE Standard for Information Technology — Systems Design — Software
Design Descriptions*, defines an SDD as the design information needed
to implement a software item.

It is not an SRS (what) and not a system architecture description
(where the item sits on the map).

## Viewpoints

1016 organizes an SDD as views. Write only the views this piece needs.

| Viewpoint | Content |
|---|---|
| Context | Design stakeholders, system boundary, requirements this design satisfies |
| Composition | Parts of the design and what each part owns |
| Logical | Static structure of classes, modules, or functions |
| Dependency | Uses and other relationships among parts |
| Information | Persistent data, schema, keys |
| Patterns | Reused design patterns |
| Interface | Provided and required interfaces |
| Interaction | Runtime scenarios among parts |
| State dynamics | States and transitions |
| Algorithm | Non-obvious processing |
| Resource | Processors, memory, stores, and how they are used |

This skill's default template uses Context, Composition, Information,
Interface, Interaction, and Resource. Add Logical, Dependency, State,
Algorithm, or Patterns only when they carry information those six miss.

## C4

[C4 component and dynamic](https://c4model.com/) diagrams fit Composition
and Interaction. Context and container diagrams belong in arc42, not
in the SDD.
